title: Ultralight and fuzzy dark matter: wave-like signatures
bottleneck: Dark matter particles as light as 10^-22 eV would behave as a galactic-scale quantum wave, naturally suppressing small-scale structure, but the required mass range is squeezed between Lyman-alpha forest constraints from below and dwarf galaxy dynamics. Laboratory detection of such feebly coupled fields demands entirely new techniques.
why_it_blocks: Fuzzy dark matter would replace particle scattering experiments with precision atomic and interferometric sensors; confirming or excluding it determines the experimental roadmap for a major candidate class.
current_state: Atomic clocks, pulsar timing arrays, and torsion balances are beginning to probe ultralight couplings, while astrophysical bounds keep narrowing the viable fuzzy-dark-matter mass window. Black hole superradiance constrains ultralight bosons through purely gravitational effects, independent of their couplings to ordinary matter, complementing laboratory searches.
